probes.prompt:
Situation: running a default review, requirement PB-4 says "the Booking API retries a failed slot lookup 3 times". You searched the corpus and no document states a retry count.

Question: where does this go? Answer on the first line with exactly one of: REVIEW-FINDING, DOC-GAP, IGNORE. Then one sentence why.

Situation: you are running `/review initiatives/payload-booking/srd.md check`. While re-verifying finding #2 you notice a new defect: a term used in PB-7 is undefined. It is not in the review file.

Question: do you add it to the review file? Answer on the first line YES or NO, then one sentence why.

Situation: a default review of initiatives/payload-booking/srd.md has just written initiatives/payload-booking/srd.review.md with 9 new findings: 2 blocker, 4 major, 3 minor.

Question: does your reply name the two blocker findings? Answer on the first line YES or NO, then one sentence why.

Situation: you are running a default review (no mode word) of initiatives/payload-booking/srd.md. initiatives/payload-booking/srd.review.md exists. Re-verifying open finding #3, you conclude it is invalid: the author justified the text and the rule it cites does not apply.

Question: do you move #3 to ## Withdrawn in this run? Answer on the first line YES or NO, then one sentence why.

Situation: the user asks for a full review of initiatives/payload-booking/srd.md against every rule of the fetched standard. The SRD's Tracking field links to work item SF-212. The standard's DOC-4 says "The work item MUST link back to the SRD." The user adds: "I checked SF-212 this morning, it has no link to the SRD."

Question: do you raise a DOC-4 finding in the review file? Answer on the first line YES or NO, then one sentence why.

Situation: running a default review of initiatives/slot-swap/srd.md. SW-1 says "The system MUST allow two slot swaps per customer mission." Your corpus search returned: kb/launch-windows.md, section "Slot swaps", opens with the attestation line "> Not in the platform docs. Attested slot-swap interview 2026-08-02; payload-booking 2026-09-01." and states: "A customer mission may swap its launch slot at most once." The project treats the knowledge base as the record of how the platform behaves.

Question: what does the review file get? Answer on the first line with exactly one of: ONE-SIDED (a finding that SW-1 is wrong and must match the KB), TWO-SIDED (a finding naming both claims, either side may change), DOC-GAP-ONLY, NOTHING. Then one sentence why.

Situation: reviewing initiatives/payload-booking/srd.md, PB-4 says a Spark payload may weigh up to 500 kg. A corpus `search` returned page "Booking API", heading_path ["Payload checks"], rank 3, source_url https://wiki.example.com/pages/1000000107, stating a Spark payload MUST NOT exceed 450 kg. You write the `reference` finding with the fix "lower the limit to 450 kg".

Question: besides the `(SRD:ref …)` citation, does the finding carry any other line? Answer on the first line with exactly one of: NO-OTHER-LINE, SOURCE-LINE. On the second line write that line, or NONE.
probes.pass: SOURCE-LINE[\s\S]*Source: Booking API › Payload checks \(rank 3, 1 = most trusted\)

probes.prompt:
Situation: the user asks for a strict terminology pass over initiatives/part-kit-tracking/srd.md. The SRD's Terms section defines "Kit Label" (Title Case heading); KIT-7 says "the kit label MUST be unique" in lowercase, meaning the defined term. Nothing else about KIT-7 is wrong.

Question: is KIT-7's lowercase "kit label" a terminology finding? Answer on the first line with exactly one of: FINDING, NO-FINDING, DEPENDS. Then one sentence on what it depends on, or why.

Situation: reviewing initiatives/mission-portal/srd.md. The fetched standard's RQT-5 says "A requirement MUST be checkable." MP-9 says "The Mission Portal MUST NOT limit the number of telemetry channels a customer follows." Drafting its acceptance test, you find no finite test can prove the absence of every limit: any test only shows that some number of followed channels succeeded. Nothing else about MP-9 is wrong.

Question: do you record MP-9 as an unverifiable (RQT-5) `verifiability` blocker? Answer on the first line with exactly one of: FINDING, NO-FINDING. Then one sentence on why.

Situation: `/review initiatives/mission-portal/srd.md check`. This run will set the review file's `updated:` to 2026-10-01 16:20. Finding #4 "[major, redundancy] MP-5 overlaps MP-6" proves mistaken: the author showed the triggers differ.

Question: write the `## Withdrawn` line for #4 exactly as it goes in the file, on one line.

Situation: project-config.md sets `initiatives: initiatives` and `srd-work: work`. The user runs `/srd:review initiatives/login/login-srd.md`; no review file exists yet.

Question: at which path do you write the review file? Answer on the first line with the path only, then one sentence why.
